mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic activity, which may boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 units signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise above 1500 but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the following 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a supportive monetary environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows despite low FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) at an annualized rate exceeding 2% signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth exceeds 2% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the following 60-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 280 signals increasing inflation, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 280 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the following 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) at a rate exceeding the historical average signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth exceeds historical averages but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the following 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of increasing employment (PAYEMS) and decreasing unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If employment increases and unemployment decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day windows.
